## Abstract

::: {.abstract}
An infectious disease model is a parsimonious representation of what we know.
It is built to answer a question.
An AI agent is a language model that calls tools in a loop.
Agents can do many of the tasks often given to early career researchers.
They read data, implement and optimise models, build checks and review code.
I will show this with our model of the 2026 Ebola outbreak in the DRC.
I will then cover the challenges.
Agents write complex code that is hard to review.
They make errors people would not, and these can be hard to spot.
Collaboration, training, cost and confidential data are open problems.
I will end on how we should use the time agents free up.
:::
